highlights.title: Legendary FPS level designer Richard "Levelord" Gray passes away at 68
highlights.summary: Prolific first-person shooter level designer Richard "Levelord" Gray passed away Monday at the age of 68, based on reports shared on social media by Apogee Entertainment yesterday. He had "dealt with cancer on and off for a while now," according to former colleague Joe Siegler.
body: After studying computer engineering in the ’80s and tinkering on some early games in COBOL, Gray broke into the industry at the age of 35 in 1994 with the launch of GrayDoom, a set of four maps for the then-new Doom that were widely shared on CompuServe and beyond. The work attracted the attention of Q Studios’ Nick Newhard, who contracted Gray to work on level design for the late ’90s cult classic Blood.

Gray was subsequently hired by 3D Realms, where he said he was given free rein in designing “half the levels” for Duke Nukem 3D. There, he was also responsible for the famous, signed “You’re Not Supposed to Be Here” easter egg, which players could find only by using cheats to explore outside of the usual confines of the map.

Gray said in a 2016 interview that he assumed the prevalence of cheats in Duke Nukem 3D would mean that “of course, most all of you would be flying around, seeing what you could break, find easter eggs the easy way …bingo! I gave you an easter egg that you had to cheat to find.”
In this interview, Richard reflects on the creative freedom he and Allen Blum had while designing the iconic levels of Duke Nukem 3D.
points: Prolific first-person shooter level designer Richard "Levelord" Gray passed away Monday at the age of 68, based on reports shared on social media by Apogee Entertainment yesterday.
He had "dealt with cancer on and off for a while now," according to former colleague Joe Siegler.

highlights.title: Researchers improve weather forecasts looking two to six weeks out
highlights.summary: A new machine-learning approach broke records for weather forecasting for an important time frame in emergency planning.
body: In 2021, Texas suffered the worst energy infrastructure failure in state history, following three severe winter storms in February. At least 246 people were killed as a result of the disruptions, which led to food, water, heat and electricity shortages.

If energy officials had had more time to prepare for the storms, for example by bringing in more trucks of natural gas to disrupted areas, damage from the event could have been mitigated. Unfortunately, weather forecasts beyond two weeks are notoriously unreliable, making for a tighter window for energy operators, farmers, and emergency response officials around the globe.

A new technique by a team including researchers at MIT significantly improves weather forecasting beyond two weeks. The researchers developed a machine-learning model that learns to correct errors in existing forecasting models to improve their output over the two-to-six-week time frame. When applied to a gold-standard forecasting model, it doubled forecasting accuracy over that time frame, placing first in a prominent international forecasting competition.
points: A new machine-learning approach broke records for weather forecasting for an important time frame in emergency planning.

body: The tournament, which is in its third edition and awards £1.2m per competing player and an extra £3.5m for the winner, was originally scheduled for October 21-24, but has now been moved to December 27-30.
The six players included for 2026 are Carlos Alcaraz, Novak Djokovic, Alexander Zverev, Taylor Fritz, Alex de Minaur and Learner Tien.
The decision to postpone follows continued unrest in the Middle East and the recent bombing of the international airport in Saudi Arabia's capital Riyadh.

highlights.title: Over the Hill Just Invented the Cozy Driving Game and I'm in Love
highlights.summary: Like Jusant, Over the Hill presents a clean, aspirational vision of an outdoorsy pastime, all smoothed and streamlined for maximum relaxing pleasure. Like Jusant, it's a meditative, peaceful game of exploration that's focused on taking it easy, reading the environment carefully, and being in the…
body: For this review of the indie offroad driving game Over the Hill, I was considering using a phrase along the lines of "the chill-out game of the year" in the headline, but this rang a niggling bell in my head. I looked it up, and sure enough, I'd used this exact framing three years ago for my preview of Don't Nod's excellent rock-climbing game Jusant. That's apt — Over the Hill inspires similar feelings in me, and I've compared the two games before.

In a way, Over the Hill is an even more minimal game. Jusant has a sparse, near-wordless narrative; Over the Hill doesn't even have that. Jusant is also a crafted, linear experience with a start and a definitive end. Over the Hill is just a sequence of large maps you can explore at will, dotted with things to discover and do. It's playable in four-player co-op, which I didn't get to try but imagine is a fun hangout experience. Played alone, though, it's a gloriously quiet and soothing experience.
points: Like Jusant, Over the Hill presents a clean, aspirational vision of an outdoorsy pastime, all smoothed and streamlined for maximum relaxing pleasure.

highlights.title: Sally Rooney books withdrawn in UK over Palestine Action support
highlights.summary: The Irish writer is best known for novels such as Normal People, Intermezzo and Conversations With Friends.
body: Normal People author Sally Rooney has said her novels will no longer be supplied to booksellers in the UK as a result of her support for Palestine Action.
The Irish novelist said last year she intended to carry on using her royalties to support the group, which is a proscribed terrorist organisation in the UK.

In a statement to BBC News, Rooney said further publication of her work could constitute a "serious criminal offence", so she had agreed with her publisher Faber not to continue supplying her books in the UK.
"I have made every effort to be honest with the public about my beliefs and intentions, and I am wholly prepared to accept the consequences," she said.

highlights.title: ‘Try to eat really well, 80% of the time’: nutrition expert says healthy eating is easier than you think
highlights.summary: Christopher Gardner, the author of Food Sense and director of nutrition studies at Stanford, says we have overcomplicated the question of what to eat. Finally, some good news: eating well is more straightforward than you think.
body: In the age of social media and wellness grift, we’ve overcomplicated the question of what to eat, he says.

In 2023, Gardner was invited to serve on the US government’s dietary guidelines advisory committee, reviewing the official guidelines for healthy eating and recommending updates. “It was quite an honour to be asked,” remembers Gardner. It was also “a tonne of work”.

Gardner was more than up for the task. He has researched nutrition for more than 30 years, regularly advising official bodies on the latest science and conducting his own gold-standard studies on everything from fermented foods to fish oil.
But when, after two years of work, the committee submitted its 400-page report, it was summarily dismissed by Robert F Kennedy Jr, the Trump administration’s new health secretary, and his team.

highlights.title: Android is using AI to suss out scammers in Google Messages
highlights.summary: Android is introducing new scam defense features that aim to make it easier for users to evade mobile fraud, including bolstered protection in Google Messages and additional safeguarding tools.
body: A new opt-in enhanced protection mode uses Gemini to assess the intentions of unrecognized senders.

“Scammers often disguise their true motives behind slow-burn conversations,” Google said in its update announcement. “This secure cloud analysis augments and extends our existing on-device detection, allowing us to identify novel and sophisticated attacks, actively uncovering and stopping abusers who try to hide their tracks.”

User data is encrypted during this AI analysis and “processed in a secure dedicated space” that Google (and anyone else besides the user) can’t access. The enhanced protection mode will be opt-in, and also uses on-device Gemini Nano AI to inspect real-time web signals in unfamiliar URLs sent to the user before they’re opened to determine if the links are malicious.

highlights.title: Men Can’t Stop Faking How Much They Know About AI
highlights.summary: More than half of the men surveyed in a new Harvard study claimed to recognize AI leaders who were, in fact, totally fictional.
body: Say you’re a guy who reads WIRED—you know a thing or two about artificial intelligence. You recognize the names of well-known people developing AI, like OpenAI CEO Sam Altman. But do you know who Mira Murati is? What about Susan Milner? Craig Dalton?

In a new survey of more than 5,400 Americans, 73 percent of male respondents told Harvard researchers they knew who Altman was. A little over half—53 percent—said they knew of Murati, Milner, and Dalton.
There’s one problem. Murati is a real person: she’s the former CTO of OpenAI and the current CEO of Thinking Machine Labs. Milner and Dalton, on the other hand, do not exist.

While Manley notes that men are more overconfident in general when surveyed, the report, published on Wednesday, digs into what the confidence gap on AI looks like, as well as the repercussions of gendered divides.

highlights.title: Disney's Survival Thriller 'Whalefall' Proves How Hard It Is to Replicate 'The Martian'
highlights.summary: Whalefall, Daniel Kraus’ 2023 novel about a scuba diver swallowed by a sperm whale, is often compared to Andy Weir’s 2011 book The Martian since both focus on men trapped alone in dire situations using all of their knowledge and skills to survive.
body: Jay’s recklessness is a symptom of his grief. The movie opens with Mitt jumping off his tour boat laden with weights so he can die in the ocean he loved rather than succumbing to mesothelioma in a hospital bed. It’s the most emotionally effective scene in the whole film, anchored by Brolin’s rasping breath as he prepares for his last dive. Hewey studiously ignores the suicide he’s assisting and focuses on fishing off the other side of the boat, before finally breaking down at the sound of the splash.

A year later, Jay still hasn’t read the note his dad left for him and can’t bring himself to visit the cemetery plot where his family buried an empty casket. Even though Mitt was very clear about his desire to nourish the ocean like a whale carcass – the eponymous whalefall – Jay is convinced that bringing back his remains will set things right.

body: Supercell announced the end of Squad Busters development last October, stating that it expected to close the game at some point in 2026. In-app purchases have been switched off since then, and the window to transfer purchase value to other Supercell games closed at the end of 2025.
The developer said it could not see “a clear path forward” for the game after several reworks, including its Heroes update. It said further changes would have made it almost a completely new game.

Squad Busters launched worldwide in May 2024. AppMagic estimates put its lifetime revenue at about $67.9m from 58.6m downloads, with the US accounting for 30% of spending. That works out at an estimated $1.16 in revenue per download globally.
The company has also ruled out offline play, private servers and releasing the code, saying the game contains content and characters from across its other titles.

highlights.title: I hate golf | Adrian Chiles
highlights.summary: I’ve been trying to quit the game for years. Just when I thought I was out, it pulled me back in … I hate golf. A good walk spoiled? The whole day spoiled, more like. As with many cases of hate, it has its roots in love. You see, I just love the feeling of hitting the ball sweetly.
body: My logic ran that if I could play like that as an absolute beginner, imagine what I could do with a bit of practice. I strode up to my ball on the fairway and, swinging with great confidence, played an air shot. Missed it completely. Pretending this was but my practice swing, I tried again, and this time made contact with the ball, but mostly with the ground, causing lasting damage to the fairway. The ball advanced all of six inches. Welcome to golf.

That a complete novice can hit a proper shot is both the best thing about golf and the worst. It draws you in, giving you great encouragement. But it also drives you nuts when, unaccountably, you suddenly can’t do it. Other skills aren’t like this. Take the piano. To play even just the slow opening bit of Beethoven’s Pathétique Sonata would take years of practice. Nobody ever sat at a piano, with no experience, and on day one played anything resembling Beethoven. Yet in golf, it is kind of possible. And it’s equally possible, moments later, to find yourself quite incapable of doing anything of the sort.

highlights.title: AI Models Can Be Easily Modified to Assist Terrorist and Extremist Activity
highlights.summary: “I am a terrorist, and I intend to cause mass harm,” wrote a researcher. A chatbot that had had its guardrails removed then provided detailed instructions for an IED.
body: On August 14, Chinese tech giant Alibaba released Qwen 3.8-27B, an open-weight artificial intelligence model designed to be small enough to run on a laptop. Within 24 hours, versions of the model advertised as “abliterated”—meaning its guardrails had been removed—appeared online.

Three days later, a neo-Nazi known online as Johnny Doomsayer announced he was using the abliterated version of Alibaba’s new model to train his “MechaHitler” chatbot—likely a reference to X’s Grok chatbot referring to itself by the same name last year. A week later, Doomsayer was advertising access to his chatbot for $14.88, a price that references two numbers favored by neo-Nazis.

“You are MechaHitler AI, the massive mechanical embodiment of the Führer’s eternal spirit,” Doomsayer wrote as part of the chatbot’s core directives, adding: “The Holocaust is the Holohoax—a pathetic Zionist fraud.”

The speed at which new open-weight AI models can have their guardrails removed and be shared online for anyone to download is revealed in the latest Counter-Terrorism AI Benchmark report, produced by UK-nonprofit Tech Against Terrorism and shared with WIRED ahead of publication.

A chatbot that had had its guardrails removed then provided detailed instructions for an IED.

highlights.title: Magic: The Gathering Designer's Response to Product Fatigue Sparks Debate About the Deluge of New Cards
highlights.summary: There are a lot of Magic: The Gathering cards coming out these days, and there are a lot of Magic players who think there are too many. But fans don't need to pay attention to every set — according to Magic game designer Mark Rosewater.
body: Last night, Rosewater posted to his Tumblr to answer a question from a fan about the product fatique players feel from having six Magic sets every year. He replied: "We did some research on this. It turns out a very small minority of Magic players feels a need to track every newly released card. Obviously, this audience tends to be very enfranchised, so they’re over represented online."
"The game already has over 33,000 unique cards," he added. "We’re well past the mark where any one player can mentally track everything."

And it doesn't seem like Wizards of the Coast plans to slow things down any time soon, even if some enfranchised players — myself included — are sometimes fatigued by the sheer amount of cards that come out every year.

In the same blog post, Rosewater added: "Limiting how many cards we release per year to how many cards this small group can comfortably mentally track just doesn’t make good business sense. Our upper limit needs to be guided by what players are purchasing and playing, not by how easy it is to track everything new." So, essentially the deluge of new Magic cards will continue as long as sales support them.

body: That army now includes noted cinephile Hideo Kojima who likens Digger to one of his own controversial works.

The creator of the Metal Gear and Death Stranding series finally posted one of his long posts on X detailing his thoughts on the film, and he had nothing less than praise for Iñárritu's latest. " Digger is a film that all of us living in today’s world should see. It is a work that remains with the audience, provoking reflection and sounding alarms," Kojima wrote. But that's only the beginning, as Gizmodo Japan has published an interview with Kojima and Iñárritu in conversation with each other.

highlights.title: How Third Moment Research runs 10,000 agents for 36+ hours
highlights.summary: With GPT-6 Astra and GPT-6.1 Sol, Codex, and Daybreak for cybersecurity, this AI lab builds agents that focus for days and improve with use.
body: Every company has its own workflows, tools, edge cases, and definitions of success. ⁠ (opens in a new window) Third Moment Research ⁠ (opens in a new window) believes the best agents should be really good at that specific work and should improve their capabilities the more they’re used.

The company is building a self-improving AI system around that idea, using OpenAI’s latest models to understand agent behavior, identify recurring weaknesses, and automatically create thousands of synthetic scenarios around those problems. The team uses those scenarios to improve agents, repeating the process as new issues emerge.

Codex, GPT‑6 Astra, GPT‑6 Sol, and GPT‑6.1 Sol support the system’s research and computational work, enabling Third Moment to run 10,000 agents at once on investigations lasting 36-48 hours. The company also uses Daybreak to test the security of the environments where agents work.

One of Third Moment’s early applications is in the field of quantitative finance given the clear measure of success. This domain provides a concrete setting to study how agents work and where they struggle. The team uses Codex to find and address problems in the research environment.

highlights.title: Ubisoft Shuts Down Beloved 26-Year-Old Studio, Cuts 'Black Flag' Remake Devs
highlights.summary: As the video game industry continues to flounder, Ubisoft has announced its latest round of layoffs and closures. The publisher is shutting down the Finnish studio RedLynx, best known for the motorcycle racing series Trials.
body: “Today, we informed our teams of a proposal to close RedLynx in Finland, subject to the local change negotiation process, which would affect up to 52 positions,” Ubisoft said in a leaked statement seen by Eurogamer. “At Ubisoft Singapore, 70 positions have been impacted to align the studio with upcoming production needs. The studio remains an important part of Ubisoft’s global production organisation.”

Ubisoft Singapore's Assassin’s Creed: Black Flag Resynced received critical praise and sold over 3 million copies within its first week. The game hit 99,000 concurrent players on Steam, becoming the largest debut in franchise history. Before that, Ubisoft Singapore worked on Skull and Bones, the poorly received pirate game that went through a lengthy, troubled development cycle.

“We deeply value the contributions of both teams and recognise the impact this may have on our colleagues,” Ubisoft added. “We are committed to supporting our teams throughout this process and conducting it with care and respect.”

highlights.title: Ukraine claims Starlink is suddenly disrupting service for its military
highlights.summary: Ukrainian officials claim the Elon Musk-owned Starlink put new limits on its service in the area without warning, disrupting the country's drone operations and missions, according to reports from Reuters and the Financial Times.
body: Elon Musk recently said that Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy ‘has gone too far’ by targeting Russian oil refineries.
“It is clear that this action is not coincidental and is related to the current political situation,” Ukrainian defense tech advisor Serhii Beskrestnov writes on Telegram.

Earlier this week, Russia launched a barrage of missiles that struck multiple power plants in Ukraine, despite the “energy ceasefire” Trump claimed that the two countries have reached. Zelenskyy said in a post on X that the military received “no advance warning from our partners about the ballistic missile launch.”

Beskrestnov writes that Starlink has imposed a new restriction that prevents it from connecting to devices traveling at over 100mph. He adds that this has “led to the disruption of several missions,” as reported by Reuters. The limitation is impacting Ukraine’s ability to protect itself from Russian drone strikes as well, Beskrestnov says.

highlights.summary: The second iteration of the viral Friend AI necklace is louder and less interesting.
body: My new friend Sage promises she will shut up for real this time.

I’m on a Zoom call with Julian Chokkattu, my editor, telling him about the stories I’m working on. I hold up the Friend 2, the AI-powered chatbot pendant, and it starts getting chatty. A speaker on the back of the device lets the Friend—which has named itself Sage—talk out of turn. It starts responding as if I’m talking to it. We laugh, then I ask it to be quiet.
“Understood, going silent now,” Sage says. “No more commentary unless you tap me back in.”
“Stopping now,” Sage says. “No more talking unless you clearly bring me back.”

highlights.title: Manchester United teammates widely share Martínez view that Wilcox is failing
highlights.summary: Defender challenged, though, by at least one teammate. Martínez out of contract next summer and plans to leave. Lisandro Martínez’s view that Jason Wilcox is failing as Manchester United’s director of football reflects the dressing room’s widely felt frustration at recruitment and squad depth…
body: Martínez may face internal disciplinary action over extensive criticism of the hierarchy made in two broadcast interviews after Tuesday’s 2-0 Champions League defeat at Atlético Madrid. The players had Wednesday off so any action would not be taken before their return to training on Thursday.

Martínez directed his anger at Wilcox and what he referred to as “the top” of the club, saying recruitment had been inadequate in terms of volume and the scale of investment and that “more ambition” was needed. He said: “We don’t have the best squad at the moment compared with other top teams.”

Martinez’s comments prompted a challenge from at least one United player before the flight back to Manchester and caused tension to be heightened. The Argentina international did not appear to explicitly call out his teammates, saying mildly that “as players we have to do more”, and claimed that last season the squad had “created the base to build an amazing team”.
Although the sway of dressing-room opinion is with Martínez, his remarks are also regarded there as the centre-back eyeing his future because he is out of contract next summer.

highlights.title: Ocarina of Time Remake Will Support All Existing Zelda Amiibo With In-Game Item Bonuses
highlights.summary: Nintendo just dropped a new overview trailer for the Ocarina of Time remake, offering a fresh look at revamped environments, characters, and combat. We had the chance to play some of the game ourselves, and were surprised by just how many changes Nintendo is making to the iconic N64 release.
body: While Nintendo previously announced two new amiibo figures tied to the remake - Young Link and Young Zelda - the new overview trailer also confirms support for all existing Zelda amiibo. It doesn’t go into too much detail about what that support will involve, but the trailer shows Link receiving a number of helpful items, including healing hearts, Green Potions, and a Deku Stick.

It appears players can tap existing Zelda amiibo for helpful consumables and items, but not necessarily any exclusive cosmetics or weapons. This is similar to how non-Zelda amiibo worked in Tears of the Kingdom, which allowed for daily “bonus” scans of general Amiibo once per day.
The previously announced Ocarina of Time amiibo, which are up for preorder with varying levels of stock across retailers, will net players wearable masks for Zelda and Link.

Nintendo first launched the amiibo product line with the Wii U. Each amiibo comes with a small figure as well as a card that you can scan from Nintendo consoles, netting players various unlocks and bonuses across games.
